rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem uses a lament image: the horses remain mourning for the dead, with reins drooping in grief.
rows.anchor: تظل جيادهم نوحا عليهم مقلدة أعنتها صفونا أراد نائحة عليهم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Joseph's shirt bore three signs: it was torn from behind, later restored Jacob's sight, and its undamaged state exposed the false blood story because a wolf would have torn it.
rows.anchor: حين قد من دبر وحين ألقي على وجه أبيه فارتد بصيرا وحين جاؤوا عليه بدم كذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the brothers blamed thieves, Jacob asked how they could have killed Joseph yet left the shirt, which they needed more than his death.
rows.anchor: فكيف قتلوه وتركوا قميصه وهم إلى قميصه أحوج منهم إلى قتله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Jacob said the wolf and thieves were not responsible; their own selves had embellished a deed they knew about.
rows.anchor: زينت لكم أنفسكم أمرا علمتموه عن قتادة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم والجبائي
rows.claim: They explain that the brothers made the crime easy for one another until they killed Joseph.
rows.anchor: سهل بعضكم لبعض أمرا في يوسف غير الذي فعلتموه حتى سهل عليكم فقتلتموه عن أبي مسلم والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says Jacob accused them by revelation from God; another says he inferred the truth through sound judgment and a clear mind.
rows.anchor: رد يعقوب عليهم بوحي من الله عز اسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful patience means enduring without agitation or complaining to people.
rows.anchor: فصبري صبر جميل لا جزع فيه ولا شكوى إلى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls beautiful patience better and more fitting than useless agitation.
rows.anchor: فصبر جميل أحسن وأولى من الجزع الذي لا يغني شيئا

rows.speaker: المرتضى
rows.claim: Patience is beautiful when undertaken for God's sake and in the way one is obligated to endure; Jacob's patience met that standard.
rows.anchor: إنما يكون الصبر جميلا إذا قصد به وجه الله تعالى وفعل للوجه الذي وجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob and the blameless young Joseph were tested through grief and enslavement under God's watch until relief came.
rows.anchor: البلاء نزل بيعقوب على كبره وبيوسف على صغره بلا ذنب كان منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob seeks God's help either to resist the brothers' account or to bear the bitter patience it requires; Joseph stayed in the well three days.
rows.anchor: بالله أستعين على دفع ما تصفون أو به أستعين على تحمل مرارة الصبر عليه ومكث يوسف في الجب ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone deserves worship: He created the heavens and earth from nothing, beginning with these signs because of their magnitude in power and blessing.
rows.anchor: أي أنشأهما من غير شيء وبدأ بذكرهما لعظم شأنهما في القدرة والنعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends rain and brings fruits from it as provision for people.
rows.anchor: أي بذلك الماء { من الثمرات رزقا لكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subdues ships to sail by His command, since He creates the winds that move them, and subdues rivers fed by rainwater flowing through valleys.
rows.anchor: أي بأمر الله لأنها تسير بالرياح والله هو المنشىء للرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon serve human benefit through daylight, moonlight, and ripening fruits and plants; their uninterrupted courses sustain creation.
rows.anchor: لتنتفعوا بضوء الشمس نهارا وبضوء القمر ليلا وليبلغ بها الثمار والنبات في النضج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are made useful for rest at night and seeking God's bounty by day.
rows.anchor: لتسكنوا في الليل ولتبتغوا في النهار من فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants many requests, including health, safety, wealth, children, honor, ease, and comfort, unless granting them would harm religion or another person.
rows.anchor: يسأل الله العافية فيعطى ويسأله النجاة فيعطى ويسأله الغنى فيعطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partitive min is necessary: saying God grants every request would be false because harmful requests are withheld; the sense is that He grants something from each kind requested.
rows.anchor: ودخلت من للتبعيض لأنه لو قال وآتاكم كل ما سألتموه لاقتضى أن جميع ما يسأله العبد يعطيه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says God has supplied whatever people need among themselves, as in His statement that He created everything on earth for them.
rows.anchor: فما من شيء يحتاج إليه العباد إلا وهو موجود فيما بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿma is a singular noun used in place of a verbal noun, so it is not pluralized; this shows God is the true benefactor and deserves worship.
rows.anchor: والنعمة هنا اسم أقيم مقام المصدر ولذلك لم يجمع فبين سبحانه أنه هو المنعم على الحقيقة

rows.speaker: طليق بن حبيب
rows.claim: God's claim is too weighty for servants to fulfill and His blessings too numerous to count, so they should begin and end each day repentant.
rows.anchor: إن حق الله تعالى أثقل من أن يقوم به العباد فإن نعم الله أكثر من أن تحصيها العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓalūm means greatly wronging oneself, while kaffār means repeatedly showing ingratitude for one's Lord's blessings.
rows.anchor: أي كثير الكفران لنعم ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative describes people as complaining in hardship and hoarding and withholding during prosperity; the verse's human is a particular type, as in the Sūrat al-ʿAṣr passage, not all humanity.
rows.anchor: ظلوم في الشدة يشكو ويجزع كفار في النعمة يجمع يمنع ولم يرد بالإنسان ها هنا العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to believing servants to pray follows the warning to enjoy worldly life because it replaces the threat of fire with lasting bliss and companionship with the righteous.
rows.anchor: عقب ذلك بالأمر للمؤمنين بما يوجب النعيم المقيم ومرافقة الأبرار ليكون قد عقب الوعيد بالوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse follows the mention of people setting up rivals: the one truly entitled to divinity and worship is God, creator of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر ما هم عليه من اتخاذ الأنداد لله سبحانه بين بعده أن واجب الوجود المستحق للإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes ma as an indefinite relative and supplies an omitted clause: God gave what people asked for and what they did not ask for; the omitted sense is supported by the clothing verse.
rows.anchor: فما ها هنا نكرة موصوفة والجملة صفة له وحذف الجملة المعطوفة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers open the initial alif in anī anā rabbuka; the remaining readers pronounce it with kasra.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو عمرو أني أنا ربك بفتح الألف والباقون إني بالكسر

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads li-ahlihi umkuthū with a ḍamma on the hāʾ, also in al-Qaṣaṣ; others use kasra.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة لأهله امكثوا وفي القصص أيضا بضم الهاء

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads akhtarnāka in the plural and with a shadda; the other readers have akhtartuka in the singular.
rows.anchor: وأنا مشدد مفتوح الهمزة اخترناك على الجمع والباقون لأهله بكسر الهاء وأنا اخترتك على التوحيد

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأهل الكوفة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir and the Kufans mark Ṭuwā with tanwīn, while the other readers leave it uninflected.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأهل الكوفة طوى بالتنوين والباقون بغير تنوين

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد ابن جبير
rows.claim: A non-canonical reading has akhfīhā with a fatḥa on its initial alif.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد ابن جبير أخفيها بفتح الألف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The kasra treats the speech as direct quotation after Moses is called; the fatḥa connects it to what he was called with, since calling may take a preposition.
rows.anchor: من كسر إني فلأن الكلام حكاية كأنه نودي فقيل يا موسى إني أنا ربك ومن فتح

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: For passive nūdiya, a clause cannot serve as the passive subject; an implicit pronoun must do so, or Moses can be the subject because he was already mentioned.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن يكون في نودي ضمير يقوم مقام الفاعل لأنه لا يجوز أن يقوم واحد من قوله يا موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭuwā may be declinable as the masculine name of a valley, or an adjective meaning blessed twice, like thunā and suwā; it may also take either ḍamma or kasra.
rows.anchor: أن يجعله اسم الوادي فيصرفه لأنه سمي مذكرا بمذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If uninflected, Ṭuwā may be a place or land name, or a form made indeclinable by alteration like ʿUmar; alteration can be posited even when its original form is unattested.
rows.anchor: أن يكون اسما لبقعة أو أرض فهو مذكر فيكون بمنزلة امرأة سميتها بحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural reading is supported by the Qur'an's shift from the singular mention of the Prophet's night journey to the plural We gave Moses the Book.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: وآتينا موسى الكتاب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Hamza's plural form can be parsed as wa-li-annā ikhtarnāka, with the prepositional phrase functioning as the object of fastamiʿ.
rows.anchor: أن يكون التقدير ولأنا اخترناك فاستمع فيكون الجار والمجرور في موضع نصب بقوله فاستمع

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Some interpret akhfīhā as making the Hour manifest: the form removes its khifāʾ, its covering, just as ashkaytu removes what someone complains of.
rows.anchor: قالوا معناه أظهرها قال أبو علي الغرض فيه أزيل عنها خفاءها

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The word khifāʾ can describe eyes as covers for sleep; the cited line witnesses this privative reading of akhfīhā.
rows.anchor: لقد علم الأيقاظ أخفية الكرى تزججها من حالك فاكتحالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an initial fatḥa, akhfīhā means I manifest it; Imruʾ al-Qays's line supplies a usage of khafā meaning to reveal.
rows.anchor: وأما أخفيها بفتح الألف فإنه أظهرها قال امرؤ القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhfaytu can mean either concealed or revealed, while khafaytuhu without the alif means only revealed; radā means destruction, as does taraddā.
rows.anchor: ويقال أخفيت الشيء كتمته وأظهرته جميعا وخفيته بلا ألف أظهرته لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb idh raʾā is an accusative circumstantial phrase attached to an omitted word, describing the account of Moses.
rows.anchor: إذ رأى الظرف يتعلق بمحذوف فهو في موضع النصب على الحال من حديث موسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses was jealous and avoided traveling companions; after finishing his term he left Midian with sheep, lost the dark route, his flock scattered, his fire striker failed, and his pregnant wife went into labor as he saw a distant fire.
rows.anchor: وكان موسى رجلا غيورا لا يصحب الرفقة لئلا ترى امرأته فلما قضى الأجل وفارق مدين خرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' wife was Shuʿayb's daughter, whom he had married in Midian.
rows.anchor: وهي بنت شعيب كان تزوجها بمدين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: It was a cold winter Friday night; iqāma is enduring, whereas makth is temporary.
rows.anchor: وكانت ليلة الجمعة في الشتاء والفرق بين المكث والإقامة أن الإقامة تدوم والمكث لا يدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānastu means I saw the fire, and Moses sought a flame from its great fire to warm his family.
rows.anchor: بشعلة اقتبسها من معظم النار تصطلون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finding guidance by the fire means finding someone there to show the way; alternatively it means a sign for the route, and hudā names both guidance and what guides.
rows.anchor: أي أجد على النار هاديا يدلني على الطريق

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The fire could point to a guide because a fire is never without people nearby.
rows.anchor: لأن النار لا تخلو من أهل لها وناس عندها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: As Moses approached, the fire appeared in a jujube tree; its brilliant light and vivid green amazed him before the tree called him.
rows.anchor: فإذا النار في شجرة عناب فوقف متعجبا من حسن ضوء تلك النار وشدة خضرة تلك الشجرة

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb reports that Moses heard a call from the tree, answered that he heard a voice but could not see its place, and learned by the response and a miracle that the caller was his Lord.
rows.anchor: نودي من الشجرة فقيل يا موسى فأجاب سريعا ما يدري من دعاه فقال إني أسمع صوتك ولا أرى مكانك

rows.speaker: الجبائي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: The people are asked about their deeds, their unjust worldly luxuries, and what made them deserve punishment.
rows.anchor: لكي تسألوا عن أعمالكم وعن تنعمكم في الدنيا بغير الحق وعما استحققتم به العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On seeing the torment, they regret their denial of the messengers and confess that they wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: على سبيل التندم لما رأوا العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl is falling into destruction; their cry of woe continued until they were cut down and left motionless like extinguished fire.
rows.anchor: أي لم يزالوا يقولون يا ويلنا وتلك دعواهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The people were eradicated by torment.
rows.anchor: استأصلناهم بالعذاب وأهلكناهم عن الحسن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another account says they were killed by the sword when Nebuchadnezzar killed them.
rows.anchor: بالسيف وهو قتل بخت نصر لهم عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further report identifies a Yemeni village whose people killed the prophet Ḥanẓala; Nebuchadnezzar killed and exiled them, then angels returned them so young and old alike could be killed, leaving no trace.
rows.anchor: نزلت في قرية باليمن قتلوا نبيا لهم يقال لهم حنظلة فسلط الله عليهم بخت نصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and what lies between them were created for a true purpose: to be signs and blessings and to make people eligible for reward.
rows.anchor: بل خلقناهما لغرض صحيح وهو أن يكون دلالة ونعمة وتعريضا للثواب

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: One interpretation takes amusement to mean a woman; another, from Ibn ʿAbbās, takes it to mean a child.
rows.anchor: اللهو المرأة عن الحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amusement may mean a desire that draws one toward passion; if God took wives or children, He would take them from heaven, not earth, and keep the matter from people.
rows.anchor: اللهو الذي هو داعي الهوى ونازع الشهوة والمعنى لو اتخذنا نساء أو ولدا لاتخذناه من أهل السماء

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the woman and child interpretations are close: both are called a man's two fragrant plants, and amusement originally euphemizes intercourse, then the woman who shares it.
rows.anchor: التفسيران في اللهو متقاربان لأن امرأة الرجل لهوه وولده لهوه ولذلك يقال امرأة الرجل وولده ريحانتاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers Christians' claims about Jesus and his mother: if God could take a spouse or child, He would take them from Himself, not from humans.
rows.anchor: تأويل الآية أن النصارى لما قالت في المسيح وأمه ما قالت

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وابن جريج
rows.claim: The phrase إن كنا فاعلين means that God would not do this at all.
rows.anchor: أي ما كنا فاعلين عن قتادة ومجاهد وابن جريج

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Alternatively, if God did take a wife or child, He would do so from Himself in a way inaccessible to human knowledge.
rows.anchor: لاتخذناه من عندنا بحيث لا يصل علمه إليكم عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God instead brings decisive proofs against falsehood; alternatives describe argument against doubt or faith against disbelief.
rows.anchor: معناه بل نورد الأدلة القاهرة على الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadmaghuhu means that truth overcomes and invalidates falsehood, or destroys it; zāhiq means perishing and vanishing, as Qatada explains.
rows.anchor: أي يعلوه ويبطله. وقيل: يهلكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God manifests truth with proofs and defeats falsehood, so He cannot be the one playing falsehood; the disbelievers deserve ruin for attributing spouse and child to Him.
rows.anchor: يظهر الحق بأدلته ويبطل الباطل فكيف يفعل الباطل واللعب

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز والشام
rows.claim: The Hijaz and Syrian readers pronounce the place name Layka without hamza and with fatḥa; the others read al-Ayka with hamza and genitive ending.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز والشام ليكة بالنصب غير مهموز ههنا وفي ص والباقون الأيكة بإثبات الهمزة والجر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Al-Ayka is the definite form of ayka; dropping hamza transfers its vowel to the lām, as in the cited reduced definite form, while fatḥa after the article is difficult without a proper-name analysis.
rows.anchor: الأيكة تعريف أيكة فإذا خففت الهمزة حذفتها وألقيت حركتها على اللام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Exegetes report that Layka was the name of the city to which Shuʿayb was sent.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن اسم المدينة التي أرسل إليها شعيب كان ليكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayka means a dense grove of interwoven trees; the cited poem uses the word for a grove.
rows.anchor: الأيكة الغيضة ذات الشجر الملتف والجمع الأيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhsir describes someone causing a loss in capital by short measure; its opposite is making a profit.
rows.anchor: المخسر المعرض للخسران في رأس المال بالنقصان أخسر يخسر إخسارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jibilla means the innate constitution of a thing; the word also occurs with ḍamma or without its final hāʾ, as the cited poets show.
rows.anchor: والجبلة الخليقة التي طبع عليها الشيء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the people of the Ayka as the people of Midian.
rows.anchor: وهم أهل مدين عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they were a different people from Midian and that God sent Shuʿayb to two communities.
rows.anchor: إنهم غيرهم عن قتادة وقال إن الله سبحانه أرسل شعيبا إلى أمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text does not call Shuʿayb their brother because he was from Midian, not their kin; elsewhere it calls him the brother of Midian.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل أخوهم لأنه لم يكن من نسبهم وكان من أهل مدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated formula for the prophets signals their one message: fear God, avoid sins, worship sincerely, and obey messengers; prophets are trustworthy and take no fee, avoiding a deterrent to acceptance.
rows.anchor: حكى الله سبحانه دعوة كل نبي بصيغة واحدة ولفظ واحد إشعارا بأن الحق الذي تأتي به الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give full measure means no shortfall, extending to measure, weight, length, and counting; do not be among those who reduce measures or weights.
rows.anchor: أعطوا الكيل وافيا غير ناقص ويدخل الوفاء في الكيل والوزن والذرع والعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qisṭās al-mustaqīm is a fair scale without bias, requiring both full delivery and full receipt.
rows.anchor: بالعدل الذي لا حيف فيه يعني زنوا وزنا يجمع الإيفاء والاستيفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not deprive people of their things means do not reduce their rights or withhold them; do not spread corruption, with ʿathā more severe than ruin according to Abu ʿUbayda.
rows.anchor: أي ولا تسعوا في الأرض بالفساد والعثي أشد والخراب عن أبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear the one who created you from nothing and created earlier generations.
rows.anchor: يعني وخلق الأمم المتقدمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Moses was promised all the sheep's dark-marked offspring that year, and the flock produced them all with that marking.
rows.anchor: وعده أن يعطيه تلك السنة من نتاج غنمه كل أدرع وأنها نتجت كلها درعا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Asked which daughter had invited Moses, he answered the one he married; Moses completed the longer ten-year term and married before it ended because he knew he would live to fulfill it.
rows.anchor: قال التي تزوج بها قيل فأي الأجلين قضى قال أوفاهما وأبعدهما عشر سنين

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The report says a man may stipulate two months' service for his bride's father; Moses knew the condition would be fulfilled because he knew he would remain alive.
rows.anchor: فالرجل يتزوج المرأة ويشترط لأبيها إجارة شهرين أيجوز ذلك قال إن موسى علم أنه سيتم له شرطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says their bargain is settled: the stated term is owed by him, and marrying one daughter is the stipulated return for him.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذي وصفت وشرطت علي فلك وما شرطت لي من تزويج إحداهما فلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term is whichever of eight or ten years Moses completes; he cannot be unjustly charged with more, and God witnesses their agreement, as Ibn ʿAbbās says.
rows.anchor: لا ظلم علي بأن أكلف أكثر منها وأطالب بالزيادة عليهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses fulfilled the longer term; the Prophet is reported to have answered that he fulfilled the term that was fuller and longer.
rows.anchor: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي الأجلين قضى موسى

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly advised saying Moses fulfilled the better and more generous term, and married the younger sister who had asked their father to hire him.
rows.anchor: إذا سئلت أي الأجلين قضى موسى فقل خيرهما وأبرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative omits that Moses finished his term, took his wife, and then headed toward Syria.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف وإيجاز وهو فلما قضى موسى الأجل وتسلم زوجته ثم توجه نحو الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One story says Moses received the staff from his father-in-law to protect the flock; another says Adam brought it from Paradise, Gabriel took it after Adam died, and later handed it to Moses, according to ʿIkrima.
rows.anchor: أمر الشيخ أن يعطي موسى عصا يدفع السباع عن غنمه بها

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the staff came out of Paradise with Adam; Gabriel took it after Adam died and gave it to Moses at night.
rows.anchor: خرج آدم بالعصا من الجنة فأخذها جبرائيل بعد موت آدم ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says prophets inherited the staff until Shuʿayb gave it to Moses.
rows.anchor: لم يزل الأنبياء يتوارثونها حتى وصلت إلى شعيب فأعطاها موسى

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان
rows.claim: Ibn Sinan reports from Abu ʿAbdillah that Moses' staff was a myrtle branch from Paradise, brought by Gabriel as Moses headed for Midian.
rows.anchor: كانت عصا موسى قضيب آس من الجنة أتاه به جبرائيل عليه السلام لما توجه تلقاء مدين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says an angel disguised as a man had deposited the staff with Shuʿayb; his daughter could only hold that staff despite trying to bring another, so her father gave it to Moses.
rows.anchor: كانت تلك العصا استودعها شعيبا ملك في صورة رجل فأمر ابنته أن تأتيه بعصا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Moses stayed with his father-in-law for another ten years after the agreed term, twenty years total, then got leave to return to Egypt and visit his parents and brother.
rows.anchor: مكث بعد انقضاء الأجل عند صهره عشرا أخرى فأقام عنده عشرين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Moses left after ten years with his wife and flock, avoiding the main route for fear of Syrian rulers; in a cold, dark wilderness his wife labored, the sheep scattered, and rain left him lost.
rows.anchor: لما قضى العشر سار بأهله أي بامرأته وبأولاد الغنم التي كانت له

rows.speaker: أبو بصير
rows.claim: Abu Baṣīr reports from Abu Jaʿfar that Moses, traveling with his family toward Jerusalem after the term, lost his way at night and saw a fire.
rows.anchor: لما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله نحو بيت المقدس أخطأ الطريق ليلا فرأى نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses hoped to learn the route he intended and whether he was on course; alternatively, he sought to learn whether the fire signaled welcome or danger.
rows.anchor: بخبر من الطريق الذي أريد قصده وهل أنا على صوبه أو منحرف عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadhwa means a piece of fire, or the burning end of a tree; taṣṭalūn means to warm yourselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بأصل شجرة فيها نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right side is the valley's right bank; the blessed spot is where God spoke and sent revelation, though another view says it was blessed by abundant trees, fruits, and goodness; the first is preferred.
rows.anchor: وهي البقعة التي قال الله تعالى فيها لموسى فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created speech in the tree and made it the speech's substrate, because an accident needs a place; Moses knew by miracle that the speech was God's.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى فعل الكلام فيها وجعل الشجرة محل الكلام لأن الكلام عرض يحتاج إلى محل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing God's speech without an intermediary is the highest prophetic station; God is Lord and creator of all, beyond inhabiting a place or being a body or accident.
rows.anchor: وهذه أعلى منازل الأنبياء أعني أن يسمعوا كلام الله من غير واسطة

rows.speaker: يحيى عن أبي بكر وهشام
rows.claim: These readers use the third-person ya in yarjiʿūn; the others read the second-person ta, shifting from the preceding third-person phrasing like iyyāka naʿbudu after al-ḥamdu lillāh.
rows.anchor: قرأ يرجعون بالياء يحيى عن أبي بكر وهشام والباقون بالتاء

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
rows.claim: The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read lanuthwiyannahum with tha; the others read lanubawwiʾannahum with ba.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم لنثوينهم بالثاء والباقون لنبوئنهم بالباء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The ba reading means settle them and is supported by the Qur'anic wording about Israel and Abraham; its lām may be extra, or the verb may answer Abraham's prayer with its object omitted.
rows.anchor: حجة من قرأ لنبوئنهم بالباء قوله ولقد بوأنا بني إسرائيل مبوء صدق

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The tha reading means make them dwell, supported by thāwiyan and poetry; because the verb takes a preposition, the absence of one in the verse needs explanation.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ لنثوينهم فحجته قوله وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan dislikes al-Aʿmash's reading min al-jannati ghurafan because one does not say athwaytuhu al-dāra.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعمش لنثوينهم من الجنة غرفا ولا يعجبني لأنك لا تقول أثويته الدار

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli explains al-Aʿmash's reading by positing an omitted preposition, as when one says to settle them in rooms, and cites similar deletion.
rows.anchor: ووجهه أنه كان في الأصل لنثوينهم من الجنة في غرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khālidīna is an accusative circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in the verb.
rows.anchor: نصب على الحال من الهاء والميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhīna ṣabarū may be a genitive adjective for al-ʿāmilīn, with the praised subject omitted; alternatively, an implied iḍāfa makes the patient ones' reward the omitted subject.
rows.anchor: في موضع جر صفة للعالمين ويكون المخصوص بالمدح محذوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the grammar of the following example, ka-ayyin is nominative, min dābbatin explains it, lā taḥmilu rizqahā describes the noun, and the sentence beginning Allāh is its predicate.
rows.anchor: من دابة في موضع التبيين له

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: The first verse was revealed concerning vulnerable believers in Mecca who were ordered to migrate.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآية الأولى في المستضعفين من المؤمنين بمكة أمروا بالهجرة عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse about creatures lacking stored provision concerned persecuted believers in Mecca told to migrate to Medina, who worried they had no house or property and who would feed or water them.
rows.anchor: في جماعة كانوا بمكة يؤذيهم المشركون فأمروا بالهجرة إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is expansive, so believers should flee lands where people prevent faith and sincere worship.
rows.anchor: يبعد أقطارها فاهربوا من أرض يمنعكم أهلها من الإيمان والإخلاص في عبادتي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: When God is disobeyed in the land where one lives, one should leave it for another land.
rows.anchor: إذا عصي الله في أرض أنت فيها فاخرج منها إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: A less common interpretation takes God's wide earth to mean Paradise; most exegetes instead understand the earth of migration.
rows.anchor: معناه إن أرض الجنة واسعة عن الجبائي وأكثر المفسرين على القول الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God alone and do not obey any creature in disobeying Him; the initial fa is conditional, as if a place becomes too confining, worship Him.
rows.anchor: اعبدوني خالصا ولا تطيعوا أحدا من خلقي في معصيتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers unable to practice their religion in one town are commanded to move elsewhere.
rows.anchor: إذا كانوا في بلد لا يلتئم فيه لهم أمر دينهم أن ينتقلوا عنه إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that every soul will die wherever it is makes migration easier: do not remain in polytheist territory out of fear of death; all return to God for recompense.
rows.anchor: كل نفس أحياها الله بحياة خلقها فيه ذائقة مرارة الموت بأي أرض كان فلا تقيموا بدار الشرك خوفا من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those promised rooms are the believers who migrated; God will settle them in elevated chambers beneath which rivers flow.
rows.anchor: أي لننزلنهم { من الجنة غرفا } أي علالي عاليات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes their chambers as palaces of pearl, emerald, and ruby in Paradise.
rows.anchor: لنسكننهم غرف الدر والزبرجد والياقوت ولننزلنهم قصور الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remain there through God's enduring existence; these chambers are an excellent reward for those who work for Him.
rows.anchor: نعم أجر العاملين } لله تلك الغرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They endured hardship and harm without abandoning their religion, patiently performed demanding acts of worship, and relied on God in important affairs and migration.
rows.anchor: على دينهم فلم يتركوه لشدة نالتهم وأذى لحقهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Many animals do not store their provision in advance.
rows.anchor: كم من دابة لا يكون رزقها مدخرا معدا عن الحسن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another interpretation says these creatures are too weak to carry food and eat directly with their mouths.
rows.anchor: لا تطيق حمل رزقها لضعفها وتأكل بأفواهما عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Most animals and birds eat only enough for their needs instead of storing food for the next day; humans, ants, and mice are exceptions.
rows.anchor: لا تدخر القوت لغدها إلا ابن آدم والنملة الفارة بل تأكل منه قدر كفايتها فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides both for the weak creature unable to carry provision and for people, so fear of lacking food should not prevent migration.
rows.anchor: أي يرزق تلك الدابة الضعيفة التي لا تقدر على حمل رزقها

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read lā yanfaʿu with a masculine verb; other readers use the feminine, and in Sūrat Ghāfir Nafiʿ agrees with the Kufans.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة لا ينفع بالياء والباقون بالتاء وكذلك في حم المؤمن

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The feminine verb agrees with the feminine noun maʿdhira; the masculine is also possible because the noun is not biologically feminine and a subject follows the verb after intervening material.
rows.anchor: التأنيث حسن لأن المعذرة اسم مؤنث وأما التذكير فلأن التأنيث غير حقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge and faith learned from proofs God established, so their knowledge is attributed to Him as their source.
rows.anchor: آتاهم الله العلم بما نصب لهم من الأدلة الموجبة له فنظروا فيها فحصل لهم العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their stay in God's Book means their time in the graves was fixed in God's record, through the resurrection, as in the barzakh verse and the Preserved Tablet analogy.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أن لبثكم ثابت في كتاب الله ثبته الله فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people given knowledge and faith have been identified as angels, prophets, or believers; another syntactic reading means those who know God's Book and faith.
rows.anchor: إن الذين أوتوا العلم والإيمان هم الملائكة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Zajjaj explains in God's Book as in God's knowledge recorded on the Preserved Tablet; people failed to know the resurrection in worldly life, so knowledge then will not help them.
rows.anchor: أي في علم الله المثبت في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day the wrongdoers' excuses will not benefit them or be accepted, and they will not be asked to make amends or return to the truth.
rows.anchor: فلا يمكنون من الاعتذار ولو اعتذروا لم يقبل عذرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has fully explained every kind of example in the Qur'an to call morally responsible people to monotheism and faith.
rows.anchor: بالغنا في البيان للمكلفين في هذا القرآن الذي أنزلناه على نبينا من كل مثل يدعوهم إلى التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when Muhammad brings a striking requested miracle, the disbelievers call the messengers fabricators, showing their obstinate denial of signs.
rows.anchor: أي أصحاب أباطيل وهذا أخبار عن عناد القوم وتكذيبهم بالآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals the hearts of those who do not know His oneness; the sealing and stamping are explained in Sūrat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: والطبع والختم مفسران في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad must patiently endure the disbelievers' harm: God's promise of punishment for enemies and support for him and the religion is true.
rows.anchor: بالعذاب والتنكيل لأعدائك والنصر والتأييد لك ولدينك

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Do not let doubters agitate you or provoke haste through anger, making you violate God's command to be patient and gentle.
rows.anchor: لا يحملنك كفر هؤلاء على الخفة والعجلة لشدة الغضب عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير برواية البزي
rows.claim: Al-Bazzī's Ibn Kathīr transmission varies the ya in yā bunayya: sukūn in the prohibition, kasra in annahā, and fatḥa in the prayer command.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير في رواية البزي يا بني لا تشرك بالله ساكنة الياء يا بني أنها مكسورة الياء

rows.speaker: القواس
rows.claim: The al-Qawwās transmission has sukūn in the prohibition and prayer vocatives, and kasra in annahā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ في رواية القواس يا بني لا تشرك يا بني أقم ساكنة الياء فيهما

rows.speaker: ابن فليح
rows.claim: Ibn Fulayḥ has sukūn in the first vocative, kasra in annahā, and fatḥa in the prayer vocative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن فليح يا بني لا تشرك يا بني أنها مكسورة الياء فيهما يا بني أقم مفتوحة الياء

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads yā bunayya with fatḥa throughout the Qur'an; the remaining readers use kasra throughout.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص يا بني بفتح الياء في كل القرآن والباقون بكسر الياء في كل القرآن

rows.speaker: عيسى الثقفي وبعضهم عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: A non-canonical reading has wahn with fatḥa on the hāʾ.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة عيسى الثقفي ورواية بعضهم عن أبي عمرو وهنا على وهن بفتح الهاء

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء والجحدري وقتادة ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce faṣluhu fī ʿāmayn with a fatḥa on the verb's ṣād.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الحسن بخلاف وأبي رجاء والجحدري وقتادة ويعقوب وفصله في عامين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: A reader who suppresses the yāʾ may be applying a pause form in connected speech, as in poetry that shortens jān for rhyme and then links it.
rows.anchor: من أسكن الياء في الوصل فإنه يجوز أن يكون على قول

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The kasra in yā bunayya annahā follows the form yā ghulāmi aqbil; fatḥa treats the added yāʾ as changed to an alif, like yā abati according to Abu ʿUthman.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: يا بني أنها فهو على قولك يا غلام أقبل

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The fatḥa in wahn may reflect the influence of a guttural; faṣl is broader than separation from nursing, but fiṣāl better fits this context because it specifically concerns weaning.
rows.anchor: وأما الفصل فإنه أعم من الفصال لأنه يستعمل في الرضاع وغيره والفصال ها هنا أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fa-arūnī mādhā khalaqa, mādhā functions as one accusative noun meaning what thing, the object of khalaqa, and the clause is governed by arūnī.
rows.anchor: تقديره أي شيء خلق فماذا بمنزلة اسم واحد في موضع نصب بأنه مفعول خلق

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: An ashkur lillāh can mean so that he thanks God, or can explain the command: We told him, be grateful for what We gave you.
rows.anchor: معناه لأن يشكر لله ويجوز أن تكون أن مفسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamalat-hu ummuhu is a circumstantial clause with an implied qad: the mother carries him while the person is in the state of being borne, implied by the command to honor parents.
rows.anchor: جملة في موضع النصب على الحال بإضمار قد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahnan is a verbal noun used circumstantially for an omitted tahnu; ʿalā wahn may qualify it or attach to its governing verb, while maʿrūfan qualifies an omitted noun meaning decent companionship.
rows.anchor: مصدر فعل محذوف في موضع الحال أي تهن وهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created heavens and earth prove God's creation; idols created nothing, and worshippers cannot answer this, showing their manifest departure from truth.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الذي ذكرت من السموات على عظمها وكبر حجمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After presenting proofs of God's oneness, power, and wisdom, the text introduces Luqman, to whom God gave wisdom: reason, knowledge, practice, and sound judgment.
rows.anchor: أي أعطيناه العقل والعلم والعمل به والإصابة في الأمور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes say Luqman was a wise man but not a prophet.
rows.anchor: فقيل: إنه كان حكيما ولم يكن نبيا عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: عكرمة والسدي والشعبي
rows.claim: Another group says Luqman was a prophet and interprets wisdom here as prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه كان نبيا عن عكرمة والسدي والشعبي وفسروا الحكمة هنا بالنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account describes Luqman as a dark-skinned Ethiopian with thick lips and split feet in David's time; he credited wisdom to God's decree, trustworthiness, truth, and silence about what did not concern him.
rows.anchor: إنه كان عبدا أسود حبشيا غليظ المشافر مشقوق الرجلين في زمن داود

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Luqman was Ayyub's sister's son, while Muqatil says he was Ayyub's maternal cousin.
rows.anchor: ابن أخت أيوب عن وهب. وقيل: كان ابن خالة أيوب عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says Luqman was not a prophet but a devout, reflective servant; when offered earthly judgment, he preferred safety unless commanded, knowing God would aid him, and argued that judgment is perilous and the afterlife's honor is better than worldly status.
rows.anchor: حقا أقول لم يكن لقمان نبيا ولكن كان عبدا كثير التفكر حسن اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the heavenly voices admired his speech, Luqman slept, awoke with wisdom, and thereafter advised David, who praised him as wise and spared the trial of judgment.
rows.anchor: فتعجبت الملائكة من حسن منطقه فنام نومة فأعطي الحكمة فانتبه يتكلم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's instruction to be grateful means thanking Him for the wisdom He gave Luqman.
rows.anchor: وقلنا له اشكر لله تعالى على ما أعطاك من الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever thanks God and other benefactors benefits himself, because gratitude earns reward and further blessings; God is independent of gratitude and praiseworthy in His acts.
rows.anchor: أي من يشكر نعمة الله ونعمة من أنعم عليه فإنه إنما يشكر لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīd may mean that God is praised for His acts or that He makes His creatures commend Him through His beneficence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مستحمد إلى خلقه بالإنعام عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude presupposes a prior blessing and a benefactor, so one cannot thank oneself any more than one can lend oneself; the obligation is owed to another.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا لا يصح أن يشكر الإنسان نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember when Luqman spoke to his son may attach either to the command to remember or to God's giving him wisdom.
rows.anchor: معناه واذكر يا محمد إذ قال لقمان لابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diminutive bunayya expresses tenderness and compassion, not belittlement; Luqman warns his son not to associate anything with God in worship.
rows.anchor: أي لا تعدل بالله شيئا في العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is grave injustice because injustice is withholding what is due: the polytheist denies God's due, knowledge of His oneness; it also ruins the self.
rows.anchor: أصل الظلم النقصان ومنع الواجب فمن أشرك بالله فقد منع ما وجب لله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding gratitude, God enjoins honoring parents as benefactors; their gratitude is paired with God's because He creates while they are the means of birth and upbringing.
rows.anchor: لما قدم الأمر بشكر النعمة أتبعه بالتنبيه على وجوب الشكر لكل منعم

rows.speaker: الضحاك والحسن
rows.claim: One explanation says the mother's weakness is compounded by the weakness of the father's and mother's seed.
rows.anchor: ضعف نطفة الوالد على ضعف نطفة الأم عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Pregnancy burdens the mother, and her weakness increases as the pregnancy advances; another view says her naturally weak constitution is further weakened by pregnancy.
rows.anchor: لأن الحمل يؤثر فيها فكلما ازداد الحمل ازدادت ضعفا على ضعف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Wahn ʿalā wahn can mean hardship upon hardship and effort upon effort.
rows.anchor: شدة على شدة وجهدا على جهد عن ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weaning occurs at the end of two full years, the total nursing period, as in the verse about two complete years for anyone wishing to complete nursing.
rows.anchor: وفطامه من الرضاع في انقضاء عامين لأن العامين جملة مدة الرضاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother nurses and raises her child for two years after birth, adding to her hardship; this explains the command to thank God and parents, honoring God through praise and obedience and parents through kindness and connection.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنها بعد ما تلده ترضعه عامين وتربية فتلحقها المشقة بذلك أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To God is the return is a threat: He will recompense each person according to deeds.
rows.anchor: وفيه تهديد أي إلي مرجعكم فأجازيكم على حسب أعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If parents urge idolatry, do not obey: what is unsupported by knowledge is false, but still treat them decently and gently in worldly affairs despite opposing them in religion.
rows.anchor: فإن دعواك إلى باطل { فلا تطعهما } في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Follow the way of those who turn to God, namely the Prophet and believers; all return to God's judgment, when He will disclose and repay their deeds.
rows.anchor: أي واسلك طريقة من رجع إلى طاعتي وأقبل إلي بقلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman's master asked him to slaughter a sheep and bring its two best morsels; Luqman brought the heart and tongue, saying they are best when good and worst when bad.
rows.anchor: اذبح شاة فأتني بأطيب مضغتين منها فذبح شاة وأتاه بالقلب واللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman warned that sitting too long on the toilet harms the liver, causes hemorrhoids, and heats the head; sit and rise gently, so the master wrote this wisdom on the privy door.
rows.anchor: طول الجلوس على الحاجة يفجع منه الكبد ويورث منه الباسور

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن دينار
rows.claim: On returning from travel, Luqman heard that his father, wife, sister, and brother had died; he responded respectively that he now controlled his affairs, renewed his bed, covered his nakedness, and had lost his support.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن دينار: قدم لقمان من سفر فلقي غلامه

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Asked who is worst, Luqman answered: one unconcerned that people see him doing wrong.
rows.anchor: أي الناس شر قال: الذي لا يبالي أن يراه الناس مسيئا

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: When someone called his face ugly, he asked whether the criticism was of the design or its designer.
rows.anchor: ما أقبح وجهك قال: تعتب على النقش أو على فاعل النقش

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqman watched David forge armor, praised it as good battle clothing, and said silence is wisdom few practice; David affirmed that Luqman deserved his name.
rows.anchor: وقال: نعم لبوس الحرب أنت فقال: الصمت حكم وقليل فاعله

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: A counsel in Man lā yaḥḍuruhu al-faqīh likens the world to a deep sea where many perish: make faith the ship, trust in God its sail, and piety its provisions.
rows.anchor: يا بني إن الدنيا بحر عميق وقد هلك فيها عالم كثير فاجعل سفينتك فيها الإيمان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu ʿAbdillah's travel counsel calls for necessary gear and medicine, agreeable companions except in sin, frequent consultation, smiling, sharing food, helping companions, silence, prayer, and generosity with mounts, water, and provisions.
rows.anchor: سافر بسيفك وخفك وعمامتك وخبائك وسقائك وخيوطك ومخرزك وتزود معك من الأدوية

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: His counsel says to verify advice before deciding, help and work alongside companions, heed elders, answer requests graciously, stop and deliberate when lost, and distrust solitary strangers in the wilderness as possible scouts or devils.
rows.anchor: إذا تحيرتم في الطريق فانزلوا وإذا شككتم في القصد فقفوا وتوامروا

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Travel counsel says pray as soon as prayer time begins, preferably in congregation; do not sleep on an animal except in a litter that lets the limbs relax, and feed it before yourself near home.
rows.anchor: إذا جاء وقت الصلاة فلا تؤخرها لشيء صلها واسترح منها فإنها دين

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: At a campsite choose pleasant, soft, grassy ground, pray two cycles before sitting, go far away for relieving yourself, then pray two and greet the place and its angelic residents when leaving.
rows.anchor: وإذا أردتم النزول فعليكم من بقاع الأرض بأحسنها لونا وألينها تربة وأكثرها عشبا

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Give some food away before eating if possible; recite scripture while riding, praise God while working, pray when alone, avoid traveling through the whole night, and do not raise your voice on the road.
rows.anchor: وإن استطعت أن لا تأكل طعاما حتى تبتدىء فتتصدق منه فافعل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu ʿAbdillah says Luqman received wisdom through strength in God's cause, restraint, silence, deep thought and perception, self-control, and examining lessons, not lineage, wealth, stature, or beauty.
rows.anchor: ما أوتي لقمان الحكمة لحسب ولا مال ولا بسط في جسم ولا جمال ولكنه كان رجلا قويا في أمر الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Luqman avoided frivolous conduct and worldly joy or grief, was modest, reconciled disputants, and asked about any saying he admired; he kept company with scholars and pitied judges and rulers for their trials.
rows.anchor: ولم يعبث بشيء قط ولم يره أحد من الناس على بول ولا غائط قط

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: He learned to master himself and desire, avoided rulers, used reflection to train himself, traveled only for benefit, and looked only at what concerned him; thereby he received wisdom and discernment.
rows.anchor: وكان يكثر مجالسة الفقهاء والعلماء وكان يغشى القضاة والملوك والسلاطين

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: Medinan readers use nominative mithqālu ḥabbatin; the others use the accusative.
rows.anchor: { مثقال حبة } بالرفع وقراءة الباقين بالنصب

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وأبو عمرو ونافع
rows.claim: The Kufans except ʿĀṣim, along with Abu ʿAmr and Nafiʿ, read lā tuṣāʿir with alif; the others read lā tuṣaʿʿir with a shadda.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وأبو عمرو ونافع ولا تصاعر بالألف والباقون ولا تصعر بالتشديد

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة غير يعقوب وحفص
rows.claim: These readers pluralize niʿamahu; the other readers use singular niʿmatahu.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة غير يعقوب وحفص نعمه على الجمع والباقون نعمة على الواحد

rows.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
rows.claim: A non-canonical reading has fa-takin with kasra on the kāf.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة عبد الكريم الجزري فتكن في صخرة بكسر الكاف

rows.speaker: يحيى بن عمارة وأصبغ
rows.claim: A non-canonical reading substitutes ṣād for sīn in aṣbagha ʿalaykum niʿmaẗan.
rows.anchor: وقراءة يحيى بن عمارة وأصبغ بالصاد عليكم نعمة ظاهرة وباطنة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Nominative mithqālu agrees with the semantic feminine of the measured good or evil deed, as in the cited verse; accusative instead makes the injustice, sin, or good deed the subject weighed by God.
rows.anchor: بالرفع فألحق علامة التأنيث بالفعل فلأن المثقال هو السيئة أو الحسنة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Lā tuṣaʿʿir and lā tuṣāʿir have the same sense, like the paired forms ḍaʿufa and ḍāʿafa.
rows.anchor: يشبه أن يكون لا تصعر ولا تصاعر بمعنى كما قال سيبويه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan calls lā tuṣāʿir a Hijazi dialect and lā tuṣaʿʿir a Tamimi dialect.
rows.anchor: لا تصاعر لغة أهل الحجاز ولا تصعر لغة بني تميم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda derives the expression from the camel disease ṣaʿar that twists its head and neck, evoking a proud person turning away.
rows.anchor: أصله من الصعر الذي يأخذ الإبل في رؤوسها وأعناقها

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Niʿam is the plural of niʿma and denotes many blessings, but even singular niʿma can indicate abundance, as the cited verse says.
rows.anchor: ونعم الله تعالى كثيرة والمفرد أيضا يدل على الكثرة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Neither singular nor plural is preferable for visible and hidden blessings, since both forms can describe them.
rows.anchor: فلا ترجيح فيه لإحدى القراءتين على الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's deed, good or evil, may weigh as little as a mustard seed; the pronoun in inna-hā may instead be a pronoun of the matter.
rows.anchor: معناه أن فعلة الإنسان من خير أو شر إن كانت مقدار حبة خردل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Zajjaj relates that Luqman's son asked whether God would know a seed deep in the sea; Luqman answered that even a mustard seed in a rock, heaven, or earth would be known and brought by God.
rows.anchor: يروى أن ابن لقمان سأل لقمان فقال: أرأيت الحبة تكون في مقل البحر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The rock may be a mountain, a great boulder that hides the tiny seed and makes it hard to retrieve.
rows.anchor: فتكن تلك الحبة في جبل عن قتادة والمعنى في صخرة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning heaven and earth after a rock reinforces the point even though the rock must be within earth, as the Qur'an similarly repeats creation and then specifies humankind.
rows.anchor: ذكر السماوات والأرض بعد ذكر الصخرة وإن كان لا بد وإن تكون الصخرة في الأرض على وجه التأكيد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says this rock lies below seven earths, a view the author rejects as unworthy of acceptance.
rows.anchor: هذه الصخرة ليست في السماوات ولا في الأرض هي تحت سبع أرضين وهذا قول مرغوب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings the deed on Judgment Day and requites a good or evil act of corresponding weight.
rows.anchor: يحضِرها الله يوم القيامة ويجازي عليها أي يأت بجزاء ما وازنها من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, bringing it means God knows the hidden seed and can manifest it whenever He wills, like the promise that whoever does an atom's weight of good or evil will see it.
rows.anchor: يعلمها الله فيأتي بها إذا شاء كذلك قليل العمل من خير أو شر يعلمه الله فيجازي عليه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report urges avoiding minor sins because they have a pursuer, warning against dismissing them on the grounds that one can repent later.
rows.anchor: اتقوا المحقرات من الذنوب فإن لها طالبا لا يقولن أحدكم أذنب وأستغفر الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: God is subtle in extracting the hidden deed and knows where it is; another explanation says al-Laṭīf knows hidden matters and al-Khabīr knows everything.
rows.anchor: خبير } بمستقرها عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated diminutive bunayya expresses tenderness and compassion, not contempt.
rows.anchor: إنما صغر اسمه في هذه المواضيع للرقة والشفقة لا للتحقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establish the obligatory prayer in its proper time and with its conditions; command obedience as right and forbid every rationally or legally vile act as wrong.
rows.anchor: أي أد الصلاة المفروضة في ميقاتها بشروطها

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Patience here means enduring hardship and injury incurred while commanding right and forbidding wrong.
rows.anchor: من المشقة والأذى في الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر عن علي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Alternatively, patience concerns worldly hardships and misfortunes such as illness.
rows.anchor: ما أصابك من شدائد الدنيا ومكارهها من الأمراض وغيرها عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm al-umūr may mean sound resolve to do good rather than evil, a firm prior intention; wavering contradicts resolve, and other accounts gloss it as steadfastness or strength and caution.
rows.anchor: من العقد الصحيح على فعل الحسن بدلا من القبيح والعزم الإرادة المتقدمة للفعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Do not turn your face from people in pride or disdain for someone speaking to you; the image comes from a camel disease twisting its neck, and pride is the worst disease for a person.
rows.anchor: ولا تمل وجهك من الناس تكبرا ولا تعرض عمن يكلمك استخفافا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear God's punishment by avoiding prohibitions and performing duties; speak rightly, without corruption, lies, or frivolity, with inward truth matching outward speech.
rows.anchor: اتقوا الله } أي اتقوا عقاب الله باجتناب معاصيه وفعل واجباته { وقولوا قولا سديدا } أي صوابا بريئا من الفساد

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
rows.claim: They interpret the sound word as sincere speech, namely the testimony that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وعكرمة: صادقا يعني كلمة التوحيد لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil connects the verse with the prohibition on causing harm: speak correctly and do not attribute anything unbecoming to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: هذا يتصل بالنهي عن الإيذاء أي قولوا قولا صوابا ولا تنسبوا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound speech lets God guide people kindly into a sound, straight way and enable good conduct; alternatively, it purifies and accepts their good deeds, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqatil.
rows.anchor: معناه إن فعلتم ذلك يصلح لكم أعمالكم بأن يلطف لكم فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God purifies deeds and accepts good works.
rows.anchor: يزكي أعمالكم ويتقبل حسناتكم عن ابن عباس ومقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives sins through upright words and deeds; obedience to Him and the Messenger brings great success and God's approval and honor.
rows.anchor: ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم } باستقامتكم في الأقوال والأفعال { ومن يطع الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: One view defines the trust as everything God commands people to obey and forbids them to violate.
rows.anchor: هي ما أمر الله به من طاعته ونهى عنه من معصيته عن أبي العالية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Another view defines the trust as God's legal rulings and obligations; the author says it is close to the first view.
rows.anchor: هي الأحكام والفرائض التي أوجبها الله تعالى على العباد عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وهذان القولان متقاربان

rows.speaker: السدي والضحاك
rows.claim: A further view means people's trusts and keeping covenants; it begins with Adam entrusting his family to Cain before traveling to Mecca, after which Cain betrayed him by killing Abel.
rows.anchor: هي أمانات الناس والوفاء بالعهود فأولها ائتمان آدم ابنه قابيل على أهله وولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes the presentation as addressed to the inhabitants of heavens, earth, and mountains, with a deleted possessive; they were shown the grave sin of violating God's trusts and laws, displaying human boldness and the angels' fear.
rows.anchor: المراد العرض على أهلها فحذف المضاف وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: The inhabitants refused the liability, sin, and punishment for neglecting the trust, and feared it; humankind carried it by sinning, ignorant of the consequences of betrayal.
rows.anchor: أي فأبى أهلهن أن يحملوا تركها وعقابها والمأثم فيها { وأشفقن منها } أي

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Because the physical heavens, earth, and mountains cannot bear moral responsibility, the verse must mean their accountable inhabitants; bearing the trust means violating it, since angels already perform it.
rows.anchor: إذا لم يصح حمله على نفس السماوات والأرض والجبال فلا بد أن يكون المراد به أهلها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Zajjaj says a betrayer bears the trust while one who fulfills it has not; likewise, sinners bear the burden of sin.
rows.anchor: كل من خان الأمانة فقد حملها ومن لم يحمل الأمانة فقد أداها
